definitions.cverdict: CVErdict: the CVE is in the Exploited or Likely next tier at the default knob (50).
definitions.cvss7: CVSS 7 or more: the CVSS base score the site shows (from the CNA, else CISA-ADP) is 7.0 or higher.
definitions.epss10: EPSS 10% or more: the EPSS score is 0.1 or higher. A CVE without an EPSS score is not flagged.
definitions.before: Flagged before the listing: a run earlier than the one that first saw the CISA KEV listing flagged the CVE, on or before the KEV dateAdded.
definitions.same_day: Same day: flagged on the KEV dateAdded itself, before the listing appeared. Counted as 0 days, separately from earlier.
definitions.eligible: Counted: KEV additions dated since the log started, for CVEs the log saw before the listing.
definitions.lead: Lead time: the KEV dateAdded minus the day of the first flag, both read as US Eastern days (CISA's time zone), in whole days. Median and quartiles interpolate between ranks.
definitions.volume: Alert volume: the share of the CVEs a method watched or scored that it flagged.
definitions.watch: Each CVE is watched while it is in the window. A method that flags it only later is not counted.

excluded.reason: Published on or after the listing day, so no method could flag it before

signals.label: The KEV listing and the CISA-ADP KEV block
signals.note: This is the answer, so it is never evidence.

signals.label: Today's EPSS score
signals.note: EPSS reacts to the listing. Only the file from the day before is used.

signals.label: A CISA SSVC "active" that may date from the listing
signals.note: When CISA changed its part of the record after the listing day, the figures with undated evidence lower "active" to "poc" if a public exploit exists, else to "none".

signals.label: Other KEV listings for the vendor or product
signals.note: Only listings dated before the listing day.

signals.label: EPSS
signals.note: The archived EPSS file from the day before. Left out when that file could not be loaded.

signals.label: Exploit-DB
signals.note: Entries added before the listing day.

signals.label: PoC repos on GitHub
signals.note: Repos created and last changed before the listing day, so all their code is older than the listing. Repos deleted since cannot be seen.

signals.label: PoC repos changed on or after the listing day
signals.note: GitHub only gives the time of the last change, so the code may have come after the listing. These repos count only with undated evidence.

signals.label: PoC star counts
signals.note: Stars are only known for today, so a repo counts once it was 3 days old by the listing day. The figures with undated evidence also count today's stars.

signals.label: Metasploit modules
signals.note: Counted when a module was changed before the listing day, which proves it existed. Other modules count only with undated evidence.

signals.label: Nuclei templates
signals.note: The template list has no dates, so templates count only with undated evidence.

signals.label: CISA SSVC automatable and technical impact
signals.note: Counted when CISA dated the assessment at least two days before the listing, or has not changed its part of the record since. CISA often dates the update it makes for a listing with the day before, so a later date counts only with undated evidence.

signals.label: CISA SSVC exploitation ("poc" or "active")
signals.note: Counted only when CISA has not changed its part of the record since the listing day. CISA updates this value when it lists a CVE, and often dates it the day before, so its date cannot be trusted.

signals.label: CNA CVSS, CVSS exploit maturity and "exploited in the wild" text
signals.note: Counted when the CNA has not changed its part of the record since the listing day. Otherwise only with undated evidence.

signals.label: CISA-ADP CVSS (when the CNA gave none)
signals.note: Counted when CISA has not changed its part of the record since the listing day. Otherwise only with undated evidence.

signals.label: Vendor and product names, tags and description
signals.note: Used as they read today in every figure, because the earlier text cannot be read. They name the product for the KEV history check and mark likely noise, such as WordPress plugins and disputed CVEs.
